paragraphs: Simlai, the attendant of R' Yehudah the Nasi and of R' Yannai. R' Yannai was leaning on the shoulder of his attendant R' Simlai, and R' Yehudah the Nasi came toward them: Bava Batra 111a. R' Yehudah the Nasi was leaning on the shoulder of his attendant R' Simlai and said to him, “Simlai, were you not in the study hall when we permitted the oil?”: Avodah Zarah 37a. He was from Lod: there, 36a. In Jerusalem Shabbat, first chapter, halakhah 4, and Avodah Zarah, chapter 2, halakhah 9, in that matter, he is called Simlai the Southerner. Yuhasin made a separate entry for Simlai of Lod, understanding him to be someone else; but there is only one, not a second. See immediately below. R' Simlai and R' Yehudah the Nasi in R' Yehoshua ben Levi's name; some say, R' Simlai and R' Yehoshua ben Levi in R' Yehudah the Nasi's name: Bekhorot 36b. Rav Yitzhak bar Shmuel bar Marta found him expounding in Netzivin.
